title: הירח בורח מאיתנו, והיום שלנו מתארך
summary: The Moon recedes 3.8 cm/yr (lunar laser ranging to the Apollo 11 retroreflector, 1969→today): the tidal bulge carried ahead of the Moon by Earth's faster spin tugs the Moon forward into a higher orbit while braking Earth (~2.3 ms/century tidal, 1.7 net); fossil growth lines count days per year (Wells 1963: ~400 in Devonian corals; de Winter 2020: Torreites clam, 70 Myr, 372 days, 23.5-h day); George Darwin's 1879 theory; why the rate is not constant (Meyers 2018: 1.4 Gyr, 18.7 h, 340,900 km); Phobos, Beresheet's NASA retroreflector, the Hebrew calendar and the Sukkot full moon.
reviewer_verdict: PASS (2 rounds) — nits left: reviewer estimates ~45 min vs the 30-min tag (prose trimmed ~10% after round 2; same order as #19–#21); time-machine clock ring is schematic; coral lens 23 vs 25 lines is a subtle difference
